bull_bear.body: Focus on fleet expansion (core rental) and KSA market penetration. Maintaining D/E below 0.5x despite capex. No dividend specifics mentioned, reinvestment prioritized for ELEVATE 2030 plan.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Supply chain disruptions (shipping congestion/costs to KSA); Execution delays in EPC due to POCM timing; Geopolitical tension in West Asia; Diesel price volatility; Margin dilution from EPC mix.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and aggressive on expansion (doubling down on KSA despite geopolitics); Transparent on margin mix shifts; Disciplined on EPC contract selection to protect ROCE.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 'margin decline' is a mathematical artifact of adding a high-ROCE, low-margin EPC business to a high-margin rental book, not a deterioration in core operating efficiency. KSA business is already monthly EBITDA positive, faster than expected.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The Elevate 2030 capital model shifts "Asset-heavy -> Hybrid Model": FY26 achievement is "SFRPL - High ROCE asset light business complements SML asset heavy business" and the FY27 target is an explicit "Pivot to capital allocator", with strategy "Reshaping ELEVATE 2030 to focus on the capital pivot model".
- Leverage discipline: net debt to equity of 0.23, 0.19, 0.28, 0.33 and 0.47 over FY22-FY26, described as "Net Debt to Equity maintained below 0.5x"; guidance raises the "D/E Ceiling (x)" to 0.72 for FY27 and 0.76-0.80 for FY28 (Q1 FY26 0.40, Q1 FY27 0.54).
- Returns: ROCE of 6%, 16%, 21%, 17%, 15% over FY22-FY26 ("Double digit ROCE"); Q1 FY27 group ROCE 16% and ROE 15% (both marked "*ROCE & ROE as on 31-Mar-26"), with segment ROCE of 15% (Crane Rental), -6% (GCC Crane Rental) and 77% (Renewables E&C).
- Cash generation: cash profit of Rs 148 / 233 / 320 / 285 / 324 Cr over FY22-FY26, captioned "Average Rs 250 Cr+ Cash Profit in last 5 years"; Q1 FY27 group cash profit Rs 104 Cr.
- Guidance (consolidated) sets FY27 total income at Rs 1,400-1,500 Cr and FY28 at Rs 1,800-1,900 Cr, EBITDA of Rs 525-575 Cr (FY27) and Rs 650-700 Cr (FY28), against FY26 actuals of Rs 1,100 Cr income and Rs 429 Cr EBITDA; blended ROCE guided to 16.25-16.5% (FY27) and 16.5-17.0% (FY28) versus 16% in FY26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Crane Rental (65% of FY26 rev): +35% growth, 79% utilization, 2.12% blended yield (India 2.24% in Q4, KSA >4.5%). Renewables EPC (31% of FY26 rev): Revenue doubled YoY, asset-light, high ROCE (~70%), lower EBITDA margin. Project EPC (4%): Minor contribution.

business.body:
- "World's 3rd Largest crane rental engineering and heavy lift solutions provider - spanning renewables, logistics, and international markets", described elsewhere as "World's 3rd & Asia's Largest Globally Ranked Crane Rental Company (IC Index 2025)"; 37 years of legacy, parent company established 1989, ICRA A+ (Stable) credit rating.
- Customer value proposition rests on "Global top 3 with India's largest crane fleet, 600+ trained operators and 120+ maintenance experts", "industry-leading health & safety with advanced monitoring, rigorous training, and international accreditation", and "unmatched speed-to-market powered by a cutting-edge digital platform and deep OEM relationships".
- Renewables subsidiary SFRPL is framed as the "Only Stable, Well-Governed Player" whose "financial discipline creates a unique market position - generating tremendous demand in a fragmented industry", on an "18+ GW Track Record" of wind execution, 140+ projects delivered and 125+ clients served.
- Middle East arm SMMEL is pitched as "From Nation Builder to Global Builder": a "6-Nation Market" launchpad with "$1B+ Crane Rental Market", "$1.5T+ Giga projects & Global Commitments" and "10-12% CAGR Expected Market Growth", with Oil & Gas and Infra as key sectors.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Group structure] Group companies span SML (parent), Sanghvi Movers Middle East Ltd (KSA subsidiary), Sanghvi Movers Middle East Heavy Lift Ltd (Qatar, step-down subsidiary), Sanghvi Movers Botswana Pty Ltd (step-down subsidiary), Sangreen Future Renewables Pvt Ltd (renewables) and Sangreen Logistics Pvt Ltd, spanning wind energy turnkey, GCC expansion, logistics for wind assets and Africa heavy-lift.
- [Technology] Elevate 2030 technology dimension moves from "Basic apps -> Value-add IT/OT": FY26 delivered "Bots for operation; ISO 27001 certified", FY27 targets "HRMS, Power BI, CRM & AI Pilot Implementation".
- [Demand drivers] The deck maps crane-rental demand to end-market capacity growth to FY30: refinery 220 -> 300 MTPA (CAGR 8%), cement 686 -> 850 MTPA (CAGR 6%), steel 258 -> 310 MTPA (CAGR 5%), wind 56.1 -> 100 GW (CAGR 15.6%), thermal 247 -> 307 GW (CAGR 6%), nuclear 8.8 -> 22.5 GW (CAGR 27%).
- [Policy risk] Named headwinds include the "ISTS waiver cliff - waiver only for projects commissioned by Jun 2028; no extension announced - timeline risk", steel "export quotas shrinking - EU cuts steel import quotas ~47% from 1 Jul 2026", refinery "project cost escalation - HRRL Barmer cost revised Rs 43,129 cr -> Rs 79,459 cr", and cement "margin moderation ahead - ICRA sees FY27 EBITDA/t easing to Rs 820-870 (from Rs 900-950)".
- [Ownership] Shareholding as on 30th June 2026: Promoters 47%, DII 1%, FII 2%, Others 50%; free-float 53%, shares outstanding 8,65,76,000, industry classified as "Diversified Commercial Services".

deepdive.thesis: Sanghvi Movers delivered strong FY26 growth (37% revenue, 16% EBITDA) driven by 35% core rental growth and a doubling of its asset-light renewables EPC book, though blended margins compressed due to the mix shift. The strategic pivot to KSA is nearing cumulative profitability with high yields (4.5%), while a record INR 4,000 crore inquiry pipeline supports a guided 30% consolidated growth trajectory for FY27.

risks.note: Explicitly listed under MD&A THREATS: 'Heightened competitive intensity in the domestic crane rental market, which may exert pressure on yields and margins despite sustained demand.' This bears directly on the two KPIs management runs the business on - average blended yield (2.12% per month) and fleet utilisation - and the MD&A concedes the Company relied on 'value-led customer engagement, disciplined asset deployment and calibrated commercial interventions to sustain yields and margins'.
risks.risk: Competitive intensity in the domestic crane rental market

risks.note: MD&A THREATS: 'Reliance on specialised equipment imported from Germany and China exposes the Company to procurement delays, logistics risks, and potential changes in customs duties.' For an asset-heavy rental model where growth is delivered by adding high-capacity cranes, procurement lead-time or duty changes directly gate the capex programme; the MoU with Action Construction Equipment Limited for indigenously manufactured heavy cranes is the stated structural response.

MD&A THREATS: 'Delays in project execution due to seasonal factors or customer site readiness may result in 10-15% of the order book carrying over into the next financial period.' This is a quantified, recurring revenue-recognition risk on a business whose visibility case rests on the order book, and it sits alongside the Rs 165 crore of FY2025-26 capex that was itself deferred to 2026-27.
risks.risk: Execution and external delays causing order-book slippage

risks.note: MD&A THREATS and segment commentary: revenue can fluctuate in the EPC businesses because of the percentage-of-completion method, 'especially in the early stages of a project'. As the Wind EPC and Project EPC verticals are the stated diversification engines and are scaling from a low base, reported performance may vary between periods independent of underlying demand; the Company states it selects contracts on execution capability and profitability thresholds.
risks.risk: Revenue volatility in the EPC businesses under percentage-of-completion

risks.note: MD&A THREATS: 'Higher operating costs in international markets such as Saudi Arabia, driven by manpower requirements, regulatory compliance, and localisation norms, impacting overall cost structures.' The segment commentary confirms that higher manpower, logistics and maintenance costs partly offset the superior Saudi yield advantage, with the Saudi business only beginning to generate positive monthly EBITDA - so the growth engine carries a margin-dilution risk while it scales.
risks.risk: Cost structure and localisation burden in new international geographies

risks.note: A structural concentration disclosed without being labelled a risk: BRSR Section A states crane hiring services account for 93.36% of turnover (Project EPC 6.63%), exports are 0% of turnover, and international markets served are stated as 0 countries. Notwithstanding the Saudi Arabia, Botswana and Qatar entities, the disclosed revenue base is overwhelmingly one activity in one country, so a domestic capex-cycle downturn or a single-sector demand shock transmits with little offset. (BRSR item 23 and the concentration items are read from the routed BRSR pages in this bundle.)

BRSR turnover rates jumped to 42.47% for permanent employees (18.22%/30.77%/19.06% split the prior year) and 77.00% for permanent workers (2.52% prior year) in FY2025-26 - the Company attributes this to Elevate 2030 growth and expansion. Separately, BRSR material issue 7 'Operational Health & Safety' flags accident, injury and fatality risk, 'especially among temporary workers who may lack sufficient training or experience', with serious incidents capable of causing project delays and downtime. For a business whose moat is stated to be execution and safety, a >40% attrition rate is a structural capability risk.
risks.risk: Workforce attrition and occupational health & safety exposure
